الفَارُ The muscles of a man: (M, K:) also mentioned in art. فأرِ, as written with ء. (TA.) أَبْرِزْ نَارَكَ وَإِنْ هَزَلْتَ فَارَكَ [Put forth thy fire, that passengers may see it and be attracted by it, though thou make lean thy muscles,] is a saying meaning (assumed tropical:) give food though thou injure thy body [by doing so]. (M, L.) ＝
-A2- See also فَأْرٌ (with which it is syn. in other senses), in art. فأر.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
